article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 50% Indica / 50% Sativa
Genetics: Animal Face × Garlic Cocktail
Breeder: Uprising Seed Co.
THC Content: 21–25%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , beta-caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Pine, garlic, savory funk, pepper, gas, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: 400–500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Animal Cocktail sits well outside the candy-heavy direction that has shaped much of modern marijuana breeding. Instead of leading with frosting, tropical fruit, or syrupy sweetness, this cultivar builds its identity around pine, garlic, skunk, fuel, spice, and an unusual savory quality sometimes compared with roasted nuts or peanut oil. The combination is not accidental.

Uprising Seed Co. created the strain by crossing Animal Face with Garlic Cocktail, a pairing documented by the breeder itself and still reflected in commercial cuts grown from Uprising genetics. Its reputation rests on more than aroma, however. Animal Cocktail generally delivers a strong but comparatively balanced experience, beginning with noticeable cerebral stimulation before settling into a calmer physical state. That combination has helped it survive beyond the short hype cycle that claims many contemporary weed varieties.
Genetics and Lineage

The parental pairing explains much of the cultivar’s personality. Animal Face comes from Face Off OG × Animal Mints and was bred by Seed Junky Genetics , bringing intense OG-style gas, pine, skunk, potency, and dense resin production into the cross. Seed Junky’s own material identifies Animal Face as that exact pairing, while Fig Farms—responsible for selecting a notable Animal Face phenotype—likewise documents Face Off OG × Animal Mints as its lineage. The Animal side therefore gives this hybrid a forceful Kush-derived backbone rather than the soft sweetness suggested by many newer dessert cultivars.

Garlic Cocktail adds an entirely different aromatic dimension. Uprising Seed Co. bred that parent from GMO × Mimosa , a lineage also documented through the breeder’s own material. GMO contributes Chem -family funk, earth, sulfurous garlic, fuel, and substantial resin production, while Mimosa introduces brighter citrus and fruit characteristics descended from Clementine and Purple Punch. Together, these influences create a surprisingly layered genetic family tree: OG and Animal Mints traits on one side; GMO funk and citrus-oriented Mimosa genetics on the other.

Uprising’s resulting hybrid is therefore better understood as a meeting point between two powerful modern cannabis families rather than simply another balanced strain. Commercial examples from SKöRD and other growers continue to identify the plant specifically as Animal Face × Garlic Cocktail bred by Uprising Seed Co., reinforcing that lineage across the legal market.
Effects and Experience

The first part of the experience tends to announce itself mentally. Rather than immediately producing a heavy body effect, the strain can begin with an upbeat change in perception, quicker conversation, amusement, and a noticeable elevation in mood. Some people find the opening phase creative or socially engaging, particularly when the amount consumed remains moderate. Commercial descriptions of the cultivar repeatedly emphasize happy, giggly, and euphoric effects alongside its potency.

More cannabis gradually shifts the balance. Physical tension may become less noticeable, the body feels heavier, and the energetic edge begins to soften into a calmer, more settled condition. It does not necessarily produce the immediate sedation associated with old-school Afghan-type weed, which helps explain its reputation as a relatively versatile hybrid. Smaller amounts may work better in an afternoon or social setting, while a stronger session can become much more appropriate for an evening at home.

Potency should not be underestimated. Marketed flower has appeared around the low-to-mid-20% THC range, including a SKöRD example labeled at 23.26% THC and only 0.06% CBD. High-THC cannabis can also produce dry mouth, red or dry eyes, slowed reaction time, anxiety, dizziness, or temporary short-term memory impairment. For consumers without much tolerance, starting conservatively makes considerably more sense than judging dosage from the strain’s balanced-hybrid classification.
Medical Benefits

Animal Cocktail is sometimes selected by medical marijuana consumers looking for a combination of mood elevation and physical relaxation. Stress, discomfort, low mood, and difficulty unwinding are among the reasons people may gravitate toward a cultivar with this type of effect profile. Those observations are useful for describing consumer behavior, but they should not be interpreted as clinical evidence that this individual strain treats any medical disorder.

Cannabis research is much stronger at the cannabinoid level than the strain-name level. Reviews of medical cannabis for chronic pain suggest that THC-containing products may provide small improvements for some patients, but the benefits need to be weighed against side effects such as dizziness, sedation, nausea, and cognitive impairment. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health similarly notes that some THC/CBD products may reduce chronic pain in the short term while also increasing adverse effects. There are no controlled trials demonstrating that Animal Cocktail itself performs better for pain than another cannabis cultivar.

Sleep is similarly complicated. A relaxing late phase may make this hybrid attractive to people who use weed before bed, yet cannabis and sleep research does not support assuming that every sedating strain improves sleep quality. THC may reduce the amount of time required to fall asleep in some situations, while frequent or long-term use can alter sleep architecture or ultimately worsen sleep quality for certain consumers. Anyone using marijuana specifically for persistent pain, anxiety, insomnia, or another health problem should discuss the broader treatment plan with a qualified healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Animal Cocktail becomes particularly distinctive when the flower is broken apart. Pine and skunk can appear first, followed by a greasy, savory funk that draws heavily from Garlic Cocktail. Garlic, pepper, fuel, earth, and a roasted-nut character often sit underneath brighter citrus notes. Weedmaps describes prominent funky and skunky aromas with pine, garlic, and an unusual peanut-oil quality, while retailers selling Uprising-derived cuts have likewise highlighted pine, gas, garlic, and peanut-like notes.

Limonene, myrcene, and beta-caryophyllene are commonly associated with the cultivar’s terpene expression, although the actual chemistry can vary considerably between growers and individual harvests. Limonene helps explain its citrus lift; beta-caryophyllene corresponds with peppery spice; myrcene contributes earthy and musky depth. Pine-like characteristics may also indicate contributions from pinene or related aromatic compounds, but a current certificate of analysis is always more reliable than a generic strain database.

On the palate, the profile often becomes heavier than the raw aroma suggests. Pine and citrus can appear early, followed by pepper, garlic, earth, and lingering gas. Consumers looking for candy or fruit-forward cannabis may find it unusual. Those who appreciate GMO, Chem, OG, or savory Kush profiles are much more likely to understand why Animal Cocktail developed such a following.
Growing Information

Cultivation information for this strain is less standardized than its lineage, largely because Uprising’s original material has circulated through different growers and selections. Available grow data generally places flowering between roughly 56 and 70 days, with many phenotypes finishing around nine weeks. That puts it comfortably within the normal range for a modern photoperiod hybrid without requiring the long bloom cycle associated with true Haze-dominant marijuana.

Plants tend to develop a medium frame with enough stretch to benefit from early canopy management. Topping, low-stress training, and selective pruning can encourage more even light exposure across flowering sites. Resin production can become substantial, reflecting both Animal Face and Garlic Cocktail ancestry. Dense flowers also mean humidity deserves attention during late bloom. Strong airflow and a controlled environment help protect compact buds from moisture-related problems.

Published third-party estimates place indoor production near 400–500 grams per square meter, though those numbers should be treated as potential rather than a breeder guarantee. Outdoors, established plants can become considerably larger when provided with strong sun, adequate root space, and a sufficiently dry autumn. Because flowering can extend into October, growers in humid or cold northern climates should pay particular attention to late-season weather.
FAQ
Is Animal Cocktail indica or sativa?

Animal Cocktail is generally classified as a balanced hybrid, often described as close to a 50/50 indica-sativa split. Its effects reflect that balance reasonably well, combining an upbeat cerebral beginning with gradually increasing physical relaxation.
What strains make Animal Cocktail?

The original Uprising Seed Co. version is Animal Face × Garlic Cocktail. The breeder has documented that parentage directly. Animal Face itself comes from Face Off OG × Animal Mints, while Garlic Cocktail combines GMO × Mimosa.
How strong is Animal Cocktail?

It should be considered a potent strain. Many descriptions place THC in the low-to-mid-20% range, and commercial flower has tested above 23%. Actual strength depends on the individual harvest, so package laboratory results matter more than a universal strain average.
What does Animal Cocktail taste like?

Expect a savory profile dominated by pine, garlic, skunk, pepper, gas, and citrus, sometimes accompanied by an unusual nutty or peanut-oil character. The flavor is notably different from sweeter Gelato- and Runtz-derived cannabis.
How long does Animal Cocktail take to flower?

Most available cultivation information places the flowering cycle around eight to ten weeks, with approximately nine weeks being a reasonable expectation for many phenotypes. Growers should still judge maturity by trichomes, flower development, and the individual plant rather than harvesting strictly by calendar date.
Final Thoughts on Animal Cocktail

Animal Cocktail succeeds because its parents contribute genuinely different qualities. Animal Face supplies the sharp OG-influenced pine, gas, potency, and resin, while Garlic Cocktail pushes the profile toward garlic, citrus, Chem funk, and savory complexity. The result is a modern hybrid that does not need confectionery flavors to distinguish itself.

For consumers who prefer pungent marijuana with an old-school edge, this cannabis strain offers a compelling alternative to the endless stream of candy-oriented hybrids. Its cerebral-to-physical effect progression gives it more flexibility than a purely sedating indica , while the complex nose makes properly grown flower immediately recognizable. Growers should expect a moderately manageable plant, an approximately nine-week flowering cycle, good resin potential, and enough aroma during bloom to make odor control important. Above all, sourcing matters: Animal Face × Garlic Cocktail from Uprising Seed Co. is the lineage that defines the original Animal Cocktail cultivar.
